details.gold_answer: A processed-food-heavy diet typically lacks: 1) Fibre (processed = 2-5g, need 25-40g/day — leads to constipation, dysbiosis), 2) Vitamin B12 (unless fortified, mostly absent), 3) Vitamin D, 4) Omega-3 (processed oils are omega-6 heavy, inflammatory ratio), 5) Potassium (processed foods high sodium, low potassium), 6) Magnesium (refined grains lose 80% magnesium), 7) Zinc, 8) Iron (bioavailability low in processed foods). Also excess: sodium, added sugars (2-3x RDA), trans fats, omega-6 (10:1 vs 2:1 ideal ratio). Quick wins: switch 2 processed meals/week for whole foods, add 1 bowl dal+rice, 1 bowl vegetable curry, 1 piece seasonal fruit daily (ICMR-NIN 2024 Dietary Guidelines).

details.query: How much water should I drink based on my activity level?
details.gold_answer: Daily water intake recommendation for Indian adults: Men ~3.7L/day (15 cups), Women ~2.7L/day (11 cups) from all fluids including water, milk, tea, soups, and moisture in foods. In hot Indian summers, add 500-1000ml. Activity increases needs by 500-1500ml depending on intensity/duration. Thirst is a late indicator of dehydration — drink regularly even if not thirsty (ICMR-NIN 2024 RDA + Hydration Guidelines).

details.query: I am pregnant, am I getting enough folate from Indian food?
details.gold_answer: A pregnant woman needs 500 mcg of folate per day. Indian foods rich in folate include: Moong dal (mcg/100g), Spinach, Moringa leaves, and Amla. However, diet alone typically provides only 200-300 mcg/day. Supplementation of 400-500 mcg/day is recommended, especially in the first 28 days to prevent neural tube defects (ICMR-NIN 2024 Pregnancy Protocol).
